9.text: The name Čaˊačên, in its Russianized form, would be Chavantzy or

10.text: Chauntzy, which is almost identical with that of Chuvantzy. This latter tribe,

11.text: almost extinct at present, in former times lived somewhere in the country

12.text: between the Yukaghir and the Chukchee regions. It bred reindeer, and

13.text: probably was an intermediate tribe between those two. The last remnants of

14.text: the Reindeer Chuvantzy are, at the present time, assimilated with the Koryak,

15.text: and speak the Koryak language; while the fisher-people of that tribe are

16.text: Russianized. The few words of the Chuvantzy language given in the curious

17.text: book by G. Dyachkoff,¹ the native school-teacher of the village of Markova,

18.text: on the Middle Anadyr, who comes from Chuvantzy stock, are mainly Yukaghir.

19.text: There are still on the tundra to the west of the Kolyma two or three clans

20.text: of Yukaghir who to some extent breed reindeer, and are intermingled with

21.text: the Tungus. The oldest documents in the archives of Nishne-Kolymsk, dated

22.text: about 1770, mention several Yukaghir of the Khodynsky Chuvansky clan.²
